chosen.premise: Kangaskhan always sleeps standing up so it will not crush the baby in its pouch.
chosen.hook: Kangaskhan cannot lie down to sleep.
chosen.visualIdea: Show Kangaskhan standing through a night cycle while the sleeping baby remains in the pouch.
chosen.note: A highly specific, counterintuitive behavior stated directly in the Pokédex and easy to dramatize visually.

candidates.premise: A Kangaskhan baby playing alone is a warning: its nearby parent may become violently enraged if approached.
candidates.hook: If you see this baby playing alone, do not catch it.
candidates.visualIdea: A harmless-looking baby plays alone as warning markers reveal the unseen parent watching nearby.
candidates.note: Strong contradiction between harmless play and hidden danger, supported across multiple entries; slightly less concrete because the parent’s exact location is not specified.

candidates.premise: When Kangaskhan’s child leaves home after roughly three years, it is the only time the mother cries wildly.
candidates.hook: Kangaskhan has one known reason to cry.
candidates.visualIdea: The pouch empties after a three-year counter, then the mother’s cry fills the screen.
candidates.note: Emotionally powerful and unusual, but “only known reason” is a cautious interpretation of the entry saying this is the only time it is heard to cry wildly.

candidates.premise: Mega Kangaskhan is the same height but weighs 20 kilograms more than Kangaskhan.
candidates.hook: Mega Kangaskhan gets heavier without getting taller.
candidates.visualIdea: Place both forms on identical 2.2-meter height lines while the weight readout jumps from 80 to 100 kilograms.
candidates.note: A clean, verifiable 20-kilogram comparison with excellent graphics potential, but it reveals less about Kangaskhan’s defining identity than the behavioral angles.

candidates.premise: Kangaskhan’s infant can stay in its mother’s pouch until it is three years old.
candidates.hook: This Pokémon’s baby may not leave its pouch for three years.
candidates.visualIdea: A three-year timeline shows the infant remaining inside the pouch until the final reveal.
candidates.note: Distinctive Kangaskhan biology with a strong timeline visual, but “until three years old” describes rare excursions rather than proving the baby continuously remains inside.

candidates.premise: Kangaskhan will keep fighting even when badly wounded—and may brave death—to protect its offspring.
candidates.hook: Kangaskhan will not stop fighting, even when badly wounded.
candidates.visualIdea: A damage meter rises toward empty while Kangaskhan continues standing between danger and its baby.
candidates.note: Well supported and dramatic, though unwavering parental protection is a broader Pokémon trope and therefore less unique.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the chosen angle has the best combination of uniqueness, surprise, specificity, visual clarity, and direct support.
